stories.headline: Massive Himalayan floods kill hundreds across Nepal and Tibet
stories.body:
Floods caused by a glacier collapse killed hundreds of people across Nepal and Tibet. As of Sunday, 810 people died in the disaster. Nepalese authorities counted 794 dead in Nepal. Chinese authorities reported 16 dead in Tibet. NDTV reported a different count of 734 recovered bodies. Search teams reported 3,048 people missing across both regions. In Nepal, 2,502 people remain missing. In Tibet, 546 people are missing.

Nepal's disaster management authority NDRRMA said 933 workers from hydropower projects are untraced. The Independent Power Producers' Association Nepal listed 537 project workers as unaccounted for. The Nepalese Army used helicopters to airlift heavy earth-moving machinery. Machinery went to the Upper Trishuli-3A hydropower project. Rescuers needed to reach a mud-filled entry point of a tunnel. Army spokesperson Brig Gen Rajaram Basnet said rescuers found the crown head of Trishuli 3A. Teams dug a hole into the tunnel to search for survivors inside.

India's Ministry of External Affairs said rescuers saved 149 Indian nationals in Nepal. Another 275 Indian citizens remain missing in Nepal. Chinese authorities said 546 people were missing in Gyirong in Tibet. That number included 261 foreign citizens from 23 countries. Among those missing in Gyirong were 49 Indians and 104 Nepalese citizens.

India sent four relief flights carrying 68.5 tonnes of supplies to Kathmandu. India also sent a 13-member army tunnel-rescue team to Nepal. Six forensic teams from India joined the relief efforts. Recovering from the disaster could cost one-tenth of Nepal's annual economic output.

Officials and experts from Nepal and China met in Kathmandu on May 27. They discussed monitoring floods, weather hazards, and glacier threats. Twelve days before the disaster, China's World Meteorological Centre emailed Nepal. The centre warned of a monsoon depression. It also warned of potential flash floods between August 14 and 19.

claims.text: As of Sunday, 810 people had been reported dead from floods in Nepal and Tibet, including 794 in Nepal and 16 in Tibet.
Reports on NDTV noted 734 bodies recovered following the massive flood caused by a glacier collapse in Nepal and Tibet.
Search teams reported 3,048 people missing across Nepal and Tibet, with 2,502 missing in Nepal and 546 in Tibet.
Nepal's disaster management authority NDRRMA stated that 933 workers from hydropower projects were untraced, while the Independent Power Producers' Association Nepal listed 537 unaccounted for.
The Nepalese Army airlifted earth-moving machinery via helicopters to the Upper Trishuli-3A hydropower project to reach a mud-filled tunnel entry point.
Nepalese Army spokesperson Brig Gen Rajaram Basnet stated that rescuers located the crown head of Trishuli 3A and dug a hole to search for survivors inside the tunnel.
India's Ministry of External Affairs stated that 149 Indian nationals had been rescued in Nepal, while 275 Indian nationals remained missing.
Chinese authorities stated that 261 foreign nationals from 23 countries were among 546 missing in Gyirong, Tibet, including 49 Indians and 104 Nepalese.
India dispatched four relief flights carrying 68.5 tonnes of supplies to Kathmandu, along with a 13-member Indian Army tunnel-rescue team and six forensic teams.
Recovering from the Himalayan flood disaster is estimated to cost one-tenth of Nepal's annual economic output.
Officials and experts from Nepal and China met in Kathmandu on May 27 to discuss monitoring and responding to floods, weather, and glacier hazards.
Twelve days before the disaster, China's World Meteorological Centre emailed Nepal warning of a monsoon depression and potential flash floods between August 14 and 19.

stories.headline: US military strikes Iranian rocket launchers in Strait of Hormuz
stories.body:
The US military struck Iranian rocket launchers near Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz on August 30. US Central Command spokesman Cdr Tim Hawkins said Iranian forces prepared to launch rockets. The rockets carried sea mines intended for the Strait of Hormuz. IRGC spokesman Hossein Mohebbi called the strike a strategic mistake. Mohebbi promised economic and military consequences for the US. Iran's Tasnim news agency said the drone strike killed two people and injured two others.

The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations said a projectile struck an oil tanker north of Khasab on August 29. A US source reported that Iran launched missiles at US forces in Jordan. All incoming missiles were intercepted. The US and Israel started strikes on Iran on February 28, beginning a six-month war. Eighteen US service members have died during the war. Iranian officials said Iran lost about $270 billion in economic damage.

Normally, about 20% of global oil passes through the Strait of Hormuz. President Donald Trump said 24 commercial ships passed through recently. Before the war, about 130 ships passed through daily. The US military redirected 83 commercial ships and disabled three as part of a blockade.

claims.text: US military forces struck Iranian rocket launchers near Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz on August 30.
US Central Command spokesman Cdr Tim Hawkins stated that Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps forces were observed preparing to launch rockets carrying sea mines into the Strait of Hormuz.
IRGC spokesman Hossein Mohebbi called the US strike a 'strategic and fatal mistake' and vowed that the US would pay economic and military consequences.
Iran's Tasnim news agency reported that the US drone strike on Larak Island killed two people and injured two others.
The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations reported that an unknown projectile struck an oil tanker north of Khasab, Oman, on August 29.
A US source reported that Iran launched missiles targeting US forces in Jordan in apparent retaliation, with all incoming missiles intercepted.
The US and Israel initiated wide-ranging strikes on Iran on February 28, beginning a war that has lasted over six months.
Eighteen US service members have been killed since the conflict with Iran began six months prior.
Iranian officials estimated that Iran has suffered about $270 billion in direct and indirect economic damage during the conflict.
Around 20% of global oil supplies normally transit through the Strait of Hormuz.
US President Donald Trump stated that 24 commercial vessels passed through the Strait of Hormuz recently, compared to roughly 130 vessels daily before the war.
As of August 30, the US military reported redirecting 83 commercial vessels and disabling three as part of its blockade of Iranian ports.

stopped or caught before reaching a destination

stories.headline: US and Venezuela sign 25-year oil deal to refill US reserves
stories.body:
US President Donald Trump announced a new oil agreement with Venezuela to refill the US Strategic Petroleum Reserve. Trump described the deal as the biggest oil deal in world history. On August 21, the US reserve held about 290 million barrels. That level was near a 44-year low. The deal follows the US capture of former President Nicolás Maduro in January on drug charges.

Venezuelan interim President Delcy Rodríguez said the 25-year energy deal covers 17 strategic oilfields. Rodríguez said the deal targets production over 1.5 million barrels per day. The agreement involves about 65 billion barrels of Venezuelan oil reserves. Rodríguez estimated the deal could generate $209 billion in revenue based on $65 per barrel. About $19 per barrel will go directly to Venezuela.

A US official said a new company received 100-year rights to untapped Venezuelan oilfields. The company involves the US government and an unnamed private operator. It gives the US 55% of effective output. US Senator Tim Kaine called the deal corrupt. Former PDVSA head Rafael Ramírez accused the administration of betraying the homeland. Protesters marched in Caracas against foreign control.

claims.text: US President Donald Trump announced that crude oil acquired from a new deal with Venezuela will be used to refill the US Strategic Petroleum Reserve.
US President Donald Trump described the agreement as 'THE BIGGEST OIL DEAL IN WORLD HISTORY'.
As of August 21, the US Strategic Petroleum Reserve stood near a 44-year low at approximately 290 million barrels.
The bilateral agreement follows the US capture of former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro in January to face federal drug-trafficking charges in New York.
Venezuelan interim President Delcy Rodríguez stated that the 25-year energy agreement with the US covers 17 strategic oilfields and targets a production of over 1.5 million barrels per day.
The 25-year energy agreement between the US and Venezuela involves an estimated 65 billion barrels of Venezuelan oil reserves.
Delcy Rodríguez estimated the agreement could generate around $209 billion in revenue for Venezuela based on a $65 per barrel benchmark price, with roughly $19 per barrel going directly to the state.

A US official stated that a new company formed by the US government and an unnamed private operator received 100-year rights to untapped Venezuelan oilfields, providing the US 55% of effective output.
US Senator Tim Kaine criticized the oil agreement, calling the arrangement 'corruption at epic scale'.
Former PDVSA head Rafael Ramírez accused Rodríguez's administration of 'driving a dagger straight into the heart of the homeland' by handing over 65 billion barrels of reserves to the US.
Dozens of left-wing protesters marched through Caracas carrying banners opposing foreign control of Venezuelan oil resources.

stories.headline: Icelandic voters reject proposal to restart EU membership talks
stories.body:
Icelandic voters rejected a proposal to restart talks to join the European Union in a national referendum. Results showed 52.8% voted against resuming talks, while 47.2% voted in favor. The BBC reported a margin of about 12,600 votes out of over 225,000 cast. France 24 reported that around 9,500 votes separated the two sides. Voter turnout reached 82.5%, the highest in any Icelandic election since 2009.

Iceland first applied to join the EU in 2009 after a banking collapse. Talks were put on hold in 2013. Prime Minister Kristrún Frostadóttir said her government will not revisit EU membership. Frostadóttir previously said Iceland already follows 75% of EU rules. Capital city voters supported joining the EU, while rural regions voted against. Fish and marine industries make up nearly 40% of Iceland's exports. AFP reported that about 90% of fisheries companies opposed EU membership. Iceland fought the Cod Wars over fishing rights with Britain in the 1970s. European Council President António Costa said the EU respects the choice. Reform UK leader Nigel Farage congratulated voters for keeping their independence.

claims.text: In a national referendum, 52.8% of Icelandic voters rejected resuming EU accession talks while 47.2% voted in favor, with a margin of about 12,600 votes out of over 225,000 cast.
France 24 reported that around 9,500 votes separated the 52.8% 'No' side from the 47.2% 'Yes' side in Iceland's EU accession referendum.
Voter turnout for the referendum reached 82.5%, the highest in any Icelandic election since 2009.
Iceland originally applied for EU membership in 2009 following the 2008 banking collapse, but talks were put on hold in 2013.
Prime Minister Kristrún Frostadóttir stated after the referendum that the issue of EU membership would not be revisited while her government remains in office.
Prime Minister Kristrún Frostadóttir stated in a July podcast interview that Iceland already adheres to 75% of EU rules.
Referendum results showed a geographic divide, with voters in the capital city of Reykjavík supporting EU accession while rural regions voted against.
Fish and marine industries account for nearly 40% of Iceland's total exports.
According to AFP, approximately 90% of companies in Iceland's fisheries sector opposed EU membership.
Iceland fought a series of maritime disputes with Britain in the 1970s, known as the Cod Wars, over fishing rights.
European Council President António Costa informed Prime Minister Frostadóttir that the EU 'fully respects the democratic choice' of Iceland's voters.
Reform UK leader Nigel Farage congratulated Icelanders, stating they had voted 'to keep their independence'.

vocab.meaning: a direct vote by the public on a single political question

stories.headline: NASA launches Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope aboard SpaceX rocket
stories.body:
NASA launched the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope aboard a SpaceX rocket on August 30. SpaceX launched the $4.3 billion telescope from the Kennedy Space Center in Florida using a Falcon Heavy rocket. The space telescope reached orbit 10 minutes after liftoff. It is traveling on a 100-day journey to Lagrange Point 2. That point is located about 1 million miles, or 1.6 million kilometers, from Earth. The telescope will join the James Webb Space Telescope at that location.

The telescope is named after physicist Nancy Grace Roman. She served as NASA's first chief astronomer in the 1960s and its first female executive. The telescope features a field of vision 100 times larger than the Hubble and James Webb telescopes. NASA administrator Nicky Fox expects the telescope to find tens of thousands or up to 100,000 exoplanets. Its primary survey will cover more than 2 billion galaxies over more than one year. The mission has a five-year primary lifespan and could run for 10 years.

claims.text: NASA launched the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope aboard a SpaceX rocket from the Kennedy Space Center in Florida on August 30.
SpaceX launched the $4.3 billion space telescope using a Falcon Heavy rocket.
The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope reached orbit 10 minutes after liftoff.
The telescope is traveling on a 100-day journey to an orbit approximately 1 million miles from Earth.
The telescope is heading to Lagrange Point 2, located 1.6 million kilometers (1 million miles) from Earth, to join the James Webb Space Telescope.
The telescope is named after physicist Nancy Grace Roman, who served as NASA's first chief astronomer in the 1960s and its first female executive.
The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope features a field of vision 100 times larger than both the Hubble and James Webb space telescopes.
NASA administrator Nicky Fox stated that the Roman telescope is expected to discover tens of thousands or up to 100,000 new exoplanets.
The telescope's primary survey is planned to cover more than 2 billion galaxies over a period of more than one year.
The mission has a five-year primary lifespan with a goal to operate for up to 10 years.

stories.headline: Google Maps updates Lake Ontario name to Lake America for US users
stories.body:
President Donald Trump signed an executive order directing federal agencies to rename Lake Ontario as Lake America. Google updated Google Maps to show Lake America to users inside the United States. Canadian users still see Lake Ontario, while users outside both countries see both names. Apple Maps continued showing Lake Ontario to US users on August 30. Trump previously renamed the Gulf of Mexico as the Gulf of America in January 2025.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney rejected the new name. Carney said Ontario comes from a 400-year-old Wendat word meaning the lake is beautiful and great. Wendat Nation Grand Chief Pierre Picard said the order attempts to erase Indigenous history. Ontario Premier Doug Ford put up a billboard near Grimsby reading Lake Ontario Now and Always. Ford called the order something out of Saturday Night Live. New York Governor Kathy Hochul said New York State will not adopt the name. The dispute happens during a trade fight, after the US put a 50% tariff on Canadian steel. Carney walked away from trade talks on August 21.

claims.text: President Donald Trump signed an executive order directing US federal agencies to rename Lake Ontario as 'Lake America'.
Google updated Google Maps to label Lake Ontario as 'Lake America' for users located inside the United States.
Google stated that Canadian users will continue to see 'Lake Ontario' on Google Maps, while users outside the US and Canada will see both names.
Apple Maps continued to display 'Lake Ontario' for US users as of August 30.
President Trump previously issued an executive order renaming the Gulf of Mexico as the 'Gulf of America' in January 2025.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney rejected the renaming, stating that Ontario originates from a 400-year-old Wendat word meaning 'the lake is beautiful, the lake is great'.
Wendat Nation Grand Chief Pierre Picard condemned the US renaming order as an attempt to erase Indigenous history and identity.
Ontario Premier Doug Ford unveiled a two-story billboard near Grimsby, Ontario, reading 'Lake Ontario. Now and Always.'
Ontario Premier Doug Ford stated on ABC's 'This Week' that Trump's executive order was 'like something out of Saturday Night Live'.
New York Governor Kathy Hochul announced that New York State would not adopt the name 'Lake America' for the lake.
The naming dispute occurs alongside an escalating trade conflict in which the US imposed a 50% tariff on Canadian steel and Canada issued retaliatory tariffs.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney walked away from US trade negotiations on August 21, calling the proposed terms a 'bad deal'.

vocab.meaning: relating to issuing orders or running a government

stories.headline: Passenger ferry capsizes off northern Cyprus leaving eight dead
stories.body:
At least eight people died after a passenger ferry capsized off northern Cyprus on Sunday evening. More than a dozen people remain missing. Prime Minister Ünal Üstel said the high-speed Filo Jet ferry carried 259 passengers and eight crew members. Survivor Efe Multici said the vessel hit the water violently before the front left side opened. Water quickly flooded inside the ship.

The 40-meter ferry sank to a depth of 514 meters about 4 nautical miles off the coast. Civilian captain Mustafa Koc rescued about 65 passengers from the water. Üstel told Turkish broadcaster TRT that 237 people were rescued and 18 remained missing. Livemint reported that 241 people were rescued. The Turkish ambassador originally reported 172 rescued and 89 missing. Turkey deployed six navy ships, five coast guard vessels, and two helicopters. Authorities detained the captain and seven crew members during an investigation.

claims.text: At least eight people died and more than a dozen were left missing after a passenger ferry capsized off northern Cyprus.
TRNC Transport Minister Erhan Arıklı reported that the high-speed 40-meter Filo Jet ferry completely sank on Sunday evening.
Prime Minister Ünal Üstel of the self-proclaimed Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus stated the ferry carried 259 passengers and eight crew members.
Survivor Efe Multici stated that the ferry slammed violently into the water before the front left side burst open and water flooded in.
TRNC officials reported that the ferry sank to a depth of 514 meters (1,686 feet) approximately 4 nautical miles off the coast.
Civilian boat captain Mustafa Koc rescued approximately 65 passengers from the water.
TRNC Prime Minister Ünal Üstel told Turkish broadcaster TRT that 237 people had been rescued while 18 remained missing.
Livemint reported that North Cyprus authorities stated 241 people were rescued from the capsized vessel.
France 24 reported initial statements from the Turkish ambassador to Nicosia that 172 people were rescued and 89 were missing.
Turkey deployed six navy ships, five coast guard vessels, and two helicopters to assist in the search and rescue operation.
Authorities detained the ship's captain and seven crew members as part of an investigation into the disaster.

stories.headline: India and Uzbekistan form partnership and sign uranium pact
stories.body:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi met President Shavkat Mirziyoyev in Tashkent to upgrade India-Uzbekistan relations. The two leaders upgraded bilateral relations to a comprehensive strategic partnership. Modi arrived in Tashkent on August 29, 2026, for a two-day state visit. Uzbekistan was the first stop on a two-nation tour that includes a visit to Kyrgyzstan for the SCO Summit.

Modi announced a long-term deal for Uzbekistan to supply uranium to India. External affairs ministry official Sibi George said both countries are close to signing the agreement. President Mirziyoyev announced a 30-day visa-free regime for Indian citizens. NPCI International Payments signed an agreement to let Indian UPI apps scan QR codes in Uzbekistan. The agreement was signed with Uzbekistan's National Interbank Processing Centre JSC. India also announced a $1 million grant for afforestation initiatives near the Aral Sea.

India and Uzbekistan set a target of $5 billion in annual bilateral trade by 2030. Current annual trade between the two countries stands at $1.32 billion. Indian commerce ministry data shows trade reached $1.3 billion in 2025. That figure marked a 33.3% increase from the previous year. Uzbekistan thanked India for supporting its push to join the World Trade Organization.

The two countries established a foreign minister-level coordination council to direct cooperation. Officials signed 11 agreements covering culture, education, mining, Ayurveda, tourism, and Buddhist site restoration. On August 30, 2026, President Mirziyoyev gave Modi Uzbekistan's Oliy Darajali Do'stlik Order. The award is the 36th honorary award Modi has received since 2016.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi arrived in Tashkent on August 29, 2026, for a two-day state visit.
Uzbekistan was the first stop in Prime Minister Narendra Modi's two-nation tour, which also includes a visit to Kyrgyzstan for the SCO Summit.

India announced a grant of $1 million for afforestation initiatives in the Aral Sea region.

Annual trade between India and Uzbekistan stands at $1.32 billion.
Commerce ministry data shows bilateral trade between India and Uzbekistan stood at $1.3 billion in 2025, a 33.3% increase from the previous year.
Uzbekistan expressed appreciation for India's support regarding Uzbekistan's accession to the World Trade Organization.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi was conferred with Uzbekistan's Oliy Darajali Do'stlik Order on August 30, 2026.
The Oliy Darajali Do'stlik Order marks the 36th honorary award conferred upon Prime Minister Narendra Modi since 2016.

stories.headline: Cockroach Janta Party movement gains momentum as school audits expand
stories.body:
Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk said organizers of the Cockroach Janta Party movement appear to have political ambitions. Wangchuk called those ambitions normal during a podcast interview. He advised organizers to stay apolitical as a pressure group to keep trust. CJP protests previously caused former Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan to resign. The movement launched volunteer audits of government schools on August 15 to check basic facilities. It set a goal to audit 100 rural schools in two months.

Government data shows India has over one million state schools. Authorities in Maharashtra and Rajasthan objected to audits done without permission. Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath ordered school checks and police cases over misleading videos. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke criticized Prime Minister Narendra Modi for calling protesting youth Dimagi Naxal. Dipke also said the BJP believes it is bigger than the RSS. RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat stated in New York that a Hindu who opposes Muslims is not a Hindu. The CJP announced a protest march in Delhi on September 5. Retired police officer Rajendra Singh asked the Supreme Court to restrict unpermitted marches before the BRICS Summit. The 1979 Assam student movement led by AASU eventually formed a government in 1985. In 2026, the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam party led by C. Joseph Vijay formed the government in Tamil Nadu.

claims.text: Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk stated on the Prakhar Gupta Xperience podcast that Cockroach Janta Party movement organisers appeared to have political ambitions, which he called normal.
Sonam Wangchuk advised CJP organizers to maintain the platform as a neutral, apolitical pressure group to retain supporter trust.
The Cockroach Janta Party movement led protests that resulted in the resignation of former Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.
On August 15, the Cockroach Janta Party launched a campaign organizing volunteer audits of government schools to document basic facilities.
The Cockroach Janta Party set an initial goal to audit 100 rural government schools over two months.
Education Ministry data shows India has over one million government schools, accounting for nearly 70% of all schools while serving under half of the country's 247 million students.
Authorities in Maharashtra and Rajasthan objected to CJP school audits conducted without prior official permission.
Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath ordered on-the-spot checks of school facilities and directed police to register cases over misleading school videos.
Abhijeet Dipke criticized Prime Minister Narendra Modi for describing protesting Gen Z individuals as 'Dimagi Naxal'.
Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke stated that the BJP believes it has grown bigger than the RSS.
RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat stated in New York that if any Hindu thinks there should be no Muslims in Bharat, he will not remain a Hindu.
The Cockroach Janta Party announced plans for a September 5 protest march from India Gate to Delhi Police Headquarters.
Retired Delhi Police officer Rajendra Singh filed a petition in the Supreme Court seeking restrictions on unpermitted marches in Lutyens' Delhi.
The Supreme Court petition requests postponing or regulating organized demonstrations in Lutyens' Delhi until after the BRICS Summit scheduled for September 12-13.
The 1979 Assam student agitation led by AASU transformed into the Asom Gana Parishad political party, which formed the Assam government in 1985.
The Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam party, led by C. Joseph Vijay, won and formed the government in Tamil Nadu in 2026.
